days.label: Tuesday
days.text: Tuesday is the last night at Radio Bean. Seven Days reported the club's last official day of operation is Tuesday, September 8 , so Honky Tonk Tuesday with Wild Leek River ($10) at 8:30 is your final chance to dance in that room. Earlier in the evening, Main Street Landing screens 'Nacho Libre' free at 7 in the Film House, and the #NotJustFatigue documentary short plays the Screening Room at 7:30 with a remote Q&A after, RSVP required. French speakers have Pause-Café Mardi at Burlington Bay Café from 5 to 6:30, singers can join the South Burlington Community Chorus as it opens its fall season at 7 at South Burlington High School , no auditions but preregistration is required and the semester runs $105 in dues, and the Vermont Figure Drawing Collective ($20) holds its weekly drop-in session at Karma Bird House from 6 to 8. Makers can bring a sewing machine they are scared of to Sandbox's free beginner sewing class on Pine Street from 4 to 5:30. Music wise, Local Dork spins vinyl free at Foam from 6, and Lavendair with Isabel and Friends play the Monkey House in Winooski at 7:30 with no cover. Early risers can hit the Networking Coffee for Women at Hula at 8:30 AM, coffee included, and anyone who needs a reset can sit with Community Meditation at the First Unitarian Universalist Society from 5:15 to 6.

days.label: Wednesday
days.text: Wednesday, our own Pick-up Basketball [MEETUP] runs at Pomeroy Park at 5:30, always free, competitive and welcoming. Downtown, una passeggiata fills Church Street with deals found at various businesses anytime between 5 and 8 with the Italian tradition of the evening stroll, no starting point and no fixed hours, and BCA is pairing it with Art Amplified at the BCA Center from 5 to 8, with Roost.World at 5 and Paper Castles at 6:30 inside the gallery. Burlington Parks wants hands for a phragmites pull at North Beach from 3 to 6, drop in anytime, bring work gloves and closed toe shoes. SPARK Talks on psychedelics brings a community conversation to the Fletcher Free Library at 5:30, free. The All-Inclusive Dyke-Tacular takes over Doma Bar on Pine Street from 5 to 10, free to walk in. Readers can meet at Phoenix Books for Trash for the Trope at 6, a romance book club reading Lisa Kleypas's A Devil in Winter this month, and film people can take the Media Factory's free Intro to Editing with DaVinci Resolve from 6 to 8, preregister if you’re interested. Music runs all night, with the free Bluegrass Nights jam at Foam at 6, Jazz Night with Ray Vega at Hotel Vermont from 8:30 to 10:30, and rapper WAX with DJ Hoppa ($30-35) at the Higher Ground Showcase Lounge with Grieves and Robscure, doors at 7. Trivia people get the free Venetian Trivia Night at the Venetian Soda Lounge from 7 to 9, and morning people can try Nature Journaling at Rock Point at 10, by donation.

days.label: Thursday
days.text: Thursday, come hang with us up in Milton for Live Music at Maquam Winery [MEETUP] . We are meeting at 5:45, Citizen Bare starts at 6, there are food trucks, and the barn has a patio plus space inside if the rain lingers. The afternoon should clear in time for the End of Summer Swim & Hang at Oakledge [MEETUP] at 5:30, snacks and paddleboards welcome, with the host noting the day may shift with the weather. Dog people get Bark & Brew ($20) at the Humane Society in South Burlington from 5:30 to 7:30, two drinks included, with Kraemer & Kin, Four Quarters and Vermont Cider Lab pouring and Le Bon Gout on food. Comedy fans should not sleep on the first night of the Big Pond Improv Festival at Vermont Comedy Club, four separate blocks at 5, 6, 7 and 8:15 with improv teams from around the country, $10 a show . The Old North End Community Dinner is back from summer break at the ONE Community Center from 5:30 to 6:30, a tagine dinner with music from Harold Kaplan and Ben Wang, with the Ward 2 Neighborhood Planning Assembly following. South Burlington's Park Hop Brews lands at Baycrest Park from 5:30 to 7:30 with music from Jacob Green, food trucks and a free trivia night. Nature lovers can take the free Pollinator Safari at the Shelburne Farms Inn from 5 to 6:30, registration required for every person in your group, or a midday beginner hike at Red Rocks [MEETUP] at noon. At night, Bread & Butter Farm hosts The Faux Paws with Otter Creek ($20) in the barn at 7, doors at 6, Montreal noise rockers Truck Violence play Foam free at 7:30 with In Lieu of Flowers, and Caitlin Morgan's contemporary dance piece 'Wind and Unwinding' ($20) gets two showings at Main Street Landing at 6 and 8. Trivia Night runs at Four Quarters in Winooski from 6, and Pathways Vermont's Peer Support Dungeons & Dragons meets at Morgan's Place from 6 to 8, beginners wanted, first timers should contact the center before coming.
